headline: FIFA scraps private investment plan after fierce global backlash
summary: FIFA's proposal to sell a 20% stake in a new unit running its events, including the World Cup, for $4.2 billion faced widespread opposition from member associations and football bodies worldwide. The plan was ultimately abandoned due to insurmountable resistan
details: FIFA has announced it will not proceed with its proposal to sell a significant portion of its business empire to outside investors. The decision follows fierce resistance from numerous member associations and football confederations globally.

The plan aimed to raise up to $4.2 billion by selling approximately a 20% stake in a new unit. This unit would have managed FIFA events, including the lucrative World Cup, valuing the enterprise at $20 billion.

The proposal, initially revealed by The Times, immediately triggered shockwaves across international sports governance. FIFA President Gianni Infantino formally presented the plan, promising member associations upfront bonuses if approved.

An immediate revolt ensued, led by UEFA, which accused FIFA of "attempting to sell the soul of football" and threatened legal action. CONCACAF and the English FA also expressed deep concerns, while the AFC was disappointed by the lack of consultation.
Opposition intensified with EU sports chief Glenn Micallef warning FIFA to "Hands off our game," and British Prime Minister Andy Burnham stating, "Football does not belong to investors."

Despite FIFA's attempts to set deadlines for acceptance and vow to press ahead, the resistance grew. All 41 member associations of CONCACAF rejected the proposal, and UEFA threatened a World Cup boycott.

Internal dissent also emerged, with former US Soccer president Carlos Cordeiro resigning in protest, calling it "a bad deal for football." FIFA's Chief Operating Officer Kevin Lamour reportedly stated the proposal was "the project of one person."

Facing insurmountable opposition and a total disintegration of political support, Infantino issued an official statement scrapping the plan. He acknowledged that the project had created divisions that were "no longer in the interest of the objective."

headline: US and Israel preparing major attacks on Iran's energy infrastructure
summary: Reports suggest potential strikes on power plants and refineries, with US officials considering cutting off Tehran's electricity supply.
details: According to a CBS News report cited by Anadolu Agency, the US and Israel are preparing for large-scale bombing raids on Iran's energy infrastructure, potentially occurring within the week.
The report indicates that power plants and refineries are primary potential targets, and US officials are reportedly considering options to shut down electricity supply to Tehran.
President Donald Trump has stated during a cabinet meeting at Camp David that the US will hit Iran 'very hard,' aiming for a point where Iran can no longer sustain the pressure.
White House spokesperson Caroline Leavitt stated that the US will prevail and that Iran will not be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons under the Trump administration.
While Israel has been informed of the preparations and is coordinating with Washington, an Israeli official told CBS News they are not aware of a decision to restart a full-scale military operation.

The report also mentions that President Trump has not yet given the final authorization for the attacks, following discussions between Trump and Netanyahu regarding the potential for economic disaster.
caption:
US and Israel are reportedly preparing massive strikes on Iran's energy infrastructure, targeting power plants and refineries.

According to a CBS News report cited by Anadolu Agency, the US and Israel are preparing for large-scale bombing raids on Iran's energy infrastructure, potentially occurring within the week.

The report indicates that power plants and refineries are primary potential targets, and US officials are reportedly considering options to shut down electricity supply to Tehran.

President Donald Trump has stated during a cabinet meeting at Camp David that the US will hit Iran 'very hard,' aiming for a point where Iran can no longer sustain the pressure.

White House spokesperson Caroline Leavitt stated that the US will prevail and that Iran will not be allowed to acquire nuclear weapons under the Trump administration.

While Israel has been informed of the preparations and is coordinating with Washington, an Israeli official told CBS News they are not aware of a decision to restart a full-scale military operation.

The report also mentions that President Trump has not yet given the final authorization for the attacks, following discussions between Trump and Netanyahu regarding the potential for economic disaster.
